summary: Anything that sends, publishes, seeds, loads or spends against a real system: dry run is the default, apply needs a named authorization, production targets are refused unless the policy allows them, and the done output states what was not sent.

required_inputs.name: effect
required_inputs.description: What would be sent, published, written or spent, and where

required_inputs.name: target_environment
required_inputs.description: Local, staging or production, and the URL or account

required_inputs.name: authorization
required_inputs.description: For an apply or execute run: who authorized it, for what scope, with what cap

required_inputs.name: reversal
required_inputs.description: How the effect is undone, or that it cannot be

checklist.rule: The default invocation composes, screenshots or diffs and sends nothing; the apply flag is explicit and named
checklist.because: War Room poster.py --execute and reconcile --apply; Flex apply-site-content; r3cruit3r staging seeds; every one has a dry run because a default that sends has sent

checklist.rule: An apply run carries a named authorization in the input: who, scope, cap; without it the tool refuses
checklist.because: War Room AGENTS.md: live sends, publications, production data changes and migrations are not smoke tests; paid evaluations require authorization

checklist.rule: A production URL, account or DSN is refused unless the policy lists it as allowed for this effect
checklist.because: War Room MCP server defaults to the production origin; the deny list and the policy exist so a script cannot point there by accident

checklist.rule: Partial failure exits nonzero and reports the failed items; a green exit means everything applied
checklist.because: Flex quote scripts are dry-run by default and exit nonzero on failure; a script that logs errors and exits zero hid a half-applied pack

checklist.rule: The done output states what was not sent, published or written, with counts
checklist.because: War Room browser-poster: done output states the queue was not drained; a reviewer cannot tell a dry run from an apply otherwise

checklist.rule: Running apply twice produces one effect: a dedupe key, an upsert, or a marker the second run reads
checklist.because: Flex content packs upsert by key; a seed that inserts twice doubles staging data

checklist.rule: The change never installs, loads or enables a scheduler (launchd, cron, beat) as part of verification
checklist.because: War Room: launchctl load is forbidden without publishing authorization; the sync script's dry run still writes

checklist.rule: A paid effect carries a cost or row cap and stops at it; a live run over an API transport also carries a dollar cap
checklist.because: Quadratus meters against list prices; the operator ruled the cap is a stop condition on API transport

checklist.rule: Tests exercise the dry-run path with fixtures and mocked transports; no test sends
checklist.because: War Room: use fixtures and mocked services; obtain authorization when external effects are needed

done_output: mode run: dry run or apply, with the authorization line for apply
what was not sent, with counts
cost or row cap and where it stopped
stop_conditions: apply requested without a named authorization
the target is production and the policy does not allow it
reversal unknown for an irreversible effect
the task asks to install or load a scheduler

adapter_fields.name: apply_flag
adapter_fields.description: The explicit flag that enables the effect

adapter_fields.name: allowed_targets
adapter_fields.description: Environments and URLs the policy allows for this effect

adapter_fields.name: authorization_format
adapter_fields.description: How a named authorization is passed and recorded

adapter_fields.name: cost_meter
adapter_fields.description: How spend or rows are counted and capped

adapter_fields.name: forbidden_commands
adapter_fields.description: Commands never run in verification, for example launchctl load
